request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE SUMMARY:

Admission Date: [DATE]
Discharge Date: [DATE]

PATIENT INFORMATION:

Patient: [NAME]
Sex: Male
Age: 73 years old
Race: African American
ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
HOSPITAL COURSE:

The patient presented to an outside hospital with shortness of breath on exertion, orthopnea and lower extremity swelling. He had a history of HFrEF and had stopped taking his cardiac medications. The physical examination revealed signs of heart failure and an elevated troponin level. The patient was treated for ACS and transferred to our hospital for further evaluation of a left atrial mass.

Coronary angiography showed thrombotic subtotal occlusion of the ramus intermedius coronary artery branch. The patient had an echocardiogram that showed a left atrial mass and severe global hypokinesis of the left ventricle. The patient was anticoagulated with unfractionated heparin but developed biventricular thrombi. The patient underwent surgical removal of masses in the right atrium and left atrium, and a two-vessel coronary artery bypass graft was performed. An intraoperative biopsy of the left ventricle showed histopathologic evidence of amyloid deposition by Congo red staining and ATTRwt amyloidosis.

The patient's postoperative course was complicated by a cerebrovascular accident that was thought to be cardioembolic in nature. He was discharged on postoperative day 15 on chronic anticoagulation with warfarin.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:

Follow-up with your primary care physician in 1 week.
Continue taking all prescribed medications.
Maintain a low-salt diet as recommended by your physician.
Follow a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and avoiding smoking and alcohol.
Watch for signs and symptoms of heart failure, such as shortness of breath and swelling, and notify your physician immediately if they occur.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode concerns a transfer for evaluation of a left atrial mass, with ACS due to thrombotic subtotal occlusion of the ramus intermedius. The patient had CABG, removal of atrial thrombi, and a biopsy showing ATTRwt cardiac amyloidosis. The question is which condition was chiefly responsible for this episode of care.

The candidates are:
- Acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina (I21 or I20), based on the coronary occlusion with elevated troponin. The surgery was a CABG for the occluded vessel. Troponin was elevated and the occlusion was thrombotic, which fits NSTEMI (I21.4).
- Cardiac amyloidosis (E85), a new finding from the biopsy.
- Heart failure (I50).
- Intracardiac thrombus (I51.3).

The patient was transferred for the atrial mass, which turned out to be thrombus (the masses were removed from the right and left atria). However, the CABG and the coronary angiography findings point to the ACS as the main treated condition. The amyloid was an incidental biopsy finding. I'll go with the myocardial infarction, I21.

CODE: I21
